beats.narration_text: Hi, this is Liam, in for Bear. smithsonian_fetch.py brings CC0 images from the Smithsonian Institution into your Brutalist reel — one at a time, with provenance. It searches a local index, resolves the full-resolution URL through the SI API, downloads, optionally upscales with Topaz Photo AI, and shelves the result. Let me show you what it actually does.

beats.narration_text: The framing that sticks wrong is that this is just a download tool. It's not. It's a provenance pipeline: CC0-only by design, an upscale step through Topaz Photo AI when that tool is present, and a source sidecar — SI object id, credit, license, URL — written automatically next to every image. You don't track attribution; the script does it for you.

'manually' struck; 'automatically' types in (terracotta)

beats.narration_text: The pipeline is metadata-first. The index must already exist — built by smithsonian_index.py — before you fetch anything. A lookup finds the record by id or text search. Resolve calls the SI content-detail endpoint for the full-resolution CC0 URL. Download, upscale with Topaz if available, and shelve with the provenance sidecar.

beats.narration_text: Here is a text search. The script tokenizes your query — dropping stop words, short words, and domain noise like smithsonian, collection, national — then scores every record in the local index. Candidates display with their SI unit, object type, and thumbnail URL. You pick a number, or pass --yes to auto-accept the top hit.

show.event: Code card: command line appears
Search output: ranked candidates with SI unit, object_type tags
Interactive prompt: 'Enter number to fetch (or 0 to abort)'
--yes flag annotation highlighted in terracotta

$ python3 runtime/scripts/smithsonian_fetch.py "UNIVAC computer console"

Top 10 match(es) for 'UNIVAC computer console':

  [1]  nmah_12345        NMAH     UNIVAC I Console and Control Panel [computer]
         thumbnail: ids.si.edu/ids/deliveryService?id=NMAH...
  [2]  nmah_67890        NMAH     UNIVAC II Operator Console  [computer]
  [3]  nmah_11111        NMAH     UNIVAC Operations Manual    [documentation]

Enter number to fetch (or 0 to abort, or SI object id): _

# --yes flag: auto-accepts top hit (use carefully on ambiguous queries)

beats.narration_text: The ranking isn't alphabetical — it's designed. A word in the title scores four points; a token match scores two. Hardware types — computer, terminal, instrument — get a 1.5 bonus. Ephemera types — pamphlet, photograph, report — get a one-point penalty. When you search for a computer, you want the machine, not the manual. That preference is baked in.

Apparatus type bonus: +1.5 (computer, terminal, instrument…)

Stop words stripped — smithsonian, national, collection, museum

EPHEMERA_TYPES: documentation, pamphlet, manual, photograph…

beats.narration_text: Resolving the full-resolution image URL is a two-stage lookup. S3-indexed records already have the URL stored directly. API-indexed records call the SI content-detail endpoint. The script navigates the nested JSON — descriptiveNonRepeating, online_media, media array — looking for type Images and access CC0. First hit wins. Fallback: any CC0 media. If nothing is CC0, the record is skipped.

show.event: Code card: GET endpoint and JSON navigation path
CC0 access gate highlighted in terracotta
S3 fast-path annotation vs API-indexed path
Fallback: any CC0 media annotated

props.title: CC0 URL resolution — content-detail endpoint
props.code:
# API-indexed records: call content-detail for full-res URL
GET https://api.si.edu/openaccess/api/v1.0/content/{record_id}

# Navigate nested JSON:
response
  └─ content
       └─ descriptiveNonRepeating
            └─ online_media
                 └─ media[]
                      └─ type: "Images"  +  access: "CC0"  ← GATE

# S3-indexed records: image_url stored directly — skip resolve step
# Fallback: any CC0 media (any type)
# Nothing CC0 found → record skipped, None returned

beats.narration_text: Upscaling is optional. The script checks whether tpai — the Topaz Photo AI CLI — exists at its expected path. Found: it runs the upscale, then compares source and output dimensions and logs the scale ratio. If the output isn't actually larger, you see WARN. Not found: the script says so, shelves the original, and moves on. No silent failure; no hard dependency.

show.event: Heading: 'Topaz upscale: optional, graceful.'
Two paths: tpai FOUND (upscale + compare) vs tpai MISSING (shelve original)
WARN path highlighted when output not larger than source
Verdict pill: DEGRADES GRACEFULLY

props.heading: Topaz upscale: optional, graceful.
props.body:
tpai FOUND → upscale → compare dimensions → log ratio
    WARN if output_w ≤ source_w  (not actually larger)
tpai MISSING → print notice → shelve original → continue

No hard dependency. No silent failure.

beats.narration_text: Every shelved image gets a .source.txt sidecar. It records: CC0, the SI object id, the title, the institutional unit, the credit line, the source URL, and the Smithsonian Open Access license statement. When you use this image a year from now, the provenance is sitting in the same folder. The pantry intake reads it. You don't have to remember anything.

beats.narration_text: Pass --copy with a reel path and --beat B07 to move the shelved image into your reel's pantry folder. The script converts JPEG to PNG for pantry intake — pantry.py expects PNGs. After the copy it prints the next step: open the image, inspect the framing, then run pantry.py. Note: --copy requires --beat; omit the beat id and the script exits immediately with a clear message.

    --id nmah_12345 \

  Set shot.focus per the subject; sidecar is pre-filled (CC0).

# --copy without --beat:
$ python3 runtime/scripts/smithsonian_fetch.py --id nmah_12345 --copy ./reel
[si-fetch] --copy requires --beat BID   ← exits immediately

beats.narration_text: What smithsonian_fetch.py gets right: strictly CC0, provenance travels with every image, index-first design means fast local search without hammering the SI API, and Topaz upscale degrades gracefully when the tool isn't there. Where it bites: the index must be pre-built — that's a separate smithsonian_index.py step. And --yes auto-accepts the top search hit — use it carefully on ambiguous queries, because the ranker gets hardware right but isn't infallible.

beats.narration_text: Here's your prompt. Paste this into Claude with your reel folder and topic in mind. Claude reads both scripts — the indexer and the fetcher — searches for a CC0 image relevant to your topic, fetches and shelves it, and drops it into pantry with the right beat prefix. The test of success: open the .source.txt next to the shelved image and confirm it shows CC0, the correct SI object id, and a credit line that matches the Smithsonian record. If the sidecar is right, the provenance chain is intact.
